summary: Streaming silence causing retry aftershocks, long-tail failures, and billing spike for Crestview Finance
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 11:42 UTC Crestview Finance observed a class of streaming requests that returned no chunks for >30s ("streaming silence"), causing client-side retries and aggressive route-level retries which amplified load and produced duplicate completions. Impact: ~45% of real-time payments validation streams for Crestview failed to produce streaming tokens within SLO; visible user-facing delays and two downstream reconciliation timeouts. The event produced an unexpected billing delta for the customer window (estimated +14% token billing) and elevated error rates across the us-east serving pool.

Observed behavior: Certain streaming sessions initiated and returned an initial HTTP 200, then emitted zero data frames for an extended period. The client retried at the SDK level after 25s and triggered new sessions; server-side session affinity and prefix cache interactions created duplicate completions once one stream resumed. This produced both silent timeouts and duplicated outputs.

Expected behavior: Streams should begin emitting token frames within 3s for the workload distribution seen; retries should not generate duplicate completions when session resume and prefix/KV cache are still active.

Impact summary: Customer-visible latency and failed transactions; reconciliations delayed; financial risk due to timeouts; billing exposure. Customer opened an escalation with CS at 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC and requested immediate mitigation and a plan for credits and prevention.

Timeline (short): 2026-03-10 11:42 UTC — alert: streaming error rate spike for Crestview. 11:47 UTC — first CS acknowledged and created incident. 12:00 UTC — SRE enabled conservative route circuit-breaker and reduced per-route retry budget. 12:20 UTC — partial mitigation observed; silence occurrences reduced but retries continued causing billing surge. 15:10 UTC — fix deployed to streaming-proxy to enforce safe session-resume semantics and drop duplicate resume attempts. 18:00 UTC — system stabilized; customer notified.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Crestview request pattern: medium-length prompts (avg 800 tokens) with streaming=true and prefix caching enabled. 2) Send 8 concurrent sessions from same client session id and artificially delay network ingress to the second session for 25-30s. 3) Observe initial HTTP 200 with no chunk frames followed by client SDK retry and duplicate completion generation once prefix cache resumes. Note: requires production-like KV cache and session affinity to reproduce reliably.
logs: Selected excerpts: [streaming-proxy] 2026-03-10T11:42:02Z WARN session[svc-1234] emitted no-chunk for 28000ms; candidate-resume=true; prefix-eviction=false. [serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T11:43:30Z INFO request[req-9f2] kernel-selection=quantized-evm variant=candidate returned NO_DATA until KV warmup. [autoscaler] 2026-03-10T11:50:12Z INFO pool us-east scale-up triggered by retry-fanout. [billing] 2026-03-10T12:05:01Z ALERT token-accounts delta +14% over 1h window for customer crestview-finance. Full logs attached in internal archive (link in related_confluence_pages).
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Interaction between session-resume logic in streaming-proxy and partial KV cache warmup for quantized variants created a window where streams were acknowledged but emitted no token frames. Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler and retry logic amplified load (aftershock) because retries created short-lived sessions that forced extra kernel selection, increasing tail latency. Evidence: correlation between no-chunk warnings and requests routed to recently scaled-up quantized shards. Kernel mismatch traces show expensive cold-paths for a subset of requests. Reproduced in staging by toggling prefix caching and forcing delayed resume.

Mitigations tried: 1) Reduced per-route retry budget (12:00 UTC) — immediate reduction in new session creation. 2) Circuit-breaker on route to avoid routing to recently scaled nodes (12:05 UTC). 3) Streaming-proxy patch to block duplicate resume attempts while KV warmup in-flight (15:10 UTC) — definitive reduction in duplicate completions.

Follow-up confirmations: After patch, no-chunk warnings dropped to baseline; billing delta projection revised downward after reprocessing logs.
resolution_notes:
Short-term fix: deployed streaming-proxy patch to enforce single-resume-per-session until KV/prefix warmup completes; tightened route-level retry budgets; added a safeguard in autoscaler to delay routing to newly provisioned quantized nodes for 30s. Customer communicated with a summary and offered a billing credit to cover the delta (+14% window) pending audit.

Long-term actions: 1) Runtime: add explicit per-session warmup handshake to avoid ack-without-chunk states. 2) Autoscaler: implement graduated routing cooldown for new nodes. 3) SDK: expose retry suppression flag when client detects long-tail silence. 4) Create a targeted regression test in the CI harness that simulates delayed-resume scenarios and measures duplicate-output risk. 5) Update runbooks: incident detection alert for no-chunk patterns and an automated mitigation playbook.

Status: patches merged (PRs referenced above), runbook updated, customer bill credit processing initiated, and a follow-up review scheduled for 2026-03-18 to validate long-term mitigations in canary.
